title: 1954 FIFA World Cup
prose:
The fifth FIFA World Cup was staged in Switzerland from 16 June to 4 July 1954, spread across six host cities in a post-war era poised between amateurism and the early professional game. Sixteen teams were drawn into four groups of four under an unusual format: within each group the two seeded sides played only the two unseeded ones, seeds did not meet each other, and any drawn group match went to extra time. The top two from each group advanced to a straight knockout phase of quarter-finals, semi-finals, a third-place match and the final.

The tournament became the highest-scoring in World Cup history by average, with 140 goals in 26 matches, roughly 5.38 per game. Its most extravagant fixture was the Austria-Switzerland quarter-final, won 7-5 by Austria, whose 12 combined goals remain a record for a single World Cup match. Hungary's celebrated 'Golden Team', the Mighty Magyars, arrived on a long unbeaten run and underlined their favouritism by thrashing West Germany 8-3 when the sides met in the group stage. Hungary's Sandor Kocsis finished as the tournament's top scorer with 11 goals.

The two met again in the final at the Wankdorf Stadium in Bern, before a reported crowd of about 60,000. Ferenc Puskas, recovering from injury, returned to open the scoring after six minutes, and Zoltan Czibor made it 2-0 inside eight. But West Germany struck back swiftly through Max Morlock in the 10th minute and Helmut Rahn in the 18th. With the game level, Rahn settled it in the 84th minute to make it 3-2; a late Puskas 'equaliser' was disallowed for offside in a disputed call. The result, an upset over the heavily favoured Hungarians, became known as the 'Miracle of Bern' and delivered West Germany its first world title. Austria finished third and Uruguay fourth. The 1954 finals were also the first World Cup to be televised. No official best-player award existed for the tournament.
